title: Cab Calloway as the greatest education: discipline and sending money home
summary: Coming from Lucky's wild band, he watched Cab's veterans wire money home first, and Cab took him aside about his family.

story.theme_name: Getting paid: wages, tips and leaving over money
story.community_name: Quitting the band: why sidemen left

blocks.x: You came into quite an organized band, of guys who had been traveling for a long time.

The greatest education -- I must admit that. Cab Calloway, I will always feel obligated, in a way, to him, because when I joined his band, I had just left Lucky's band which was a wild band, I mean, when I say, 'wild', guys were not oriented as far as being family men, and a lot of them in the band were married, but they were just like they were single.

But when I joined Cab, I watched the other guys in the band, and I watched the way they used to send money home, because I used to forget to send money home some weeks, because I used to love to gamble, which I didn't know how to gamble, but I still loved to gamble, and I used to lose my money a lot of times, but I noticed guys like Jonah Jones and Milt Henton and Keg Johnson and Hilton Jefferson, these guys, how they would run to the Western Union and send that money home first, and then they would gamble the rest.

Then I had Cab one day to sit down and talk to me, and he told me, he says, "You know, you can do anything you want to do, but it's the way you do it. Now you're a married man and you got a wife and kid, and you're staying out ..." -- and I didn't even know that the man was

even watching me or paying attention to me, even, to what I was doing, and he sat down and talked to me and I finally started to understand and realize that I was married, because I got married very young -- I was 19 when I got married, and I guess there were a whole lot of things that I was supposed to do that I didn't do before I got married, and I was trying to do these things.
